summary: Verified the non-blocking 'Structuring in process' banner on the Decision Desk. Logged in as demo owner, submitted the required __UITEST__ text directive, skipped clarify panel, and observed that the sticky banner (data-testid='structuring-banner') with status 'Structuring in process…' (data-testid='structuring-status') appeared, remained visible during processing, did NOT block interaction (scroll + inbox filter chip click succeeded while banner was showing), and cleared cleanly on completion. The Execution Summary dialog with real task/assignee/approval counts opened immediately after the banner disappeared.
critical_code_review_comments: Inbox.js is now 549 lines — approaching the recommended 700-line soft limit. Consider extracting EscalationCard, PendingApprovalCard, and the CaptureBox into their own components to keep the file focused (informational, not blocking).
procLabel derivation ternary chain is fine but could be a small map lookup for readability (minor).
seed_data_creation: One __UITEST__ decision was created via the text-directive path (main agent will clean it up per instructions).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Non-blocking structuring banner works. Observed status sequence and timings: banner first became visible ~4.7s after clicking 'Structure it' (this delay is the clarify precheck + skip roundtrip), remained visible ~6.0s showing only 'Structuring in process…' (queued/transcribing stages were too fast to be captured for the text-directive path — which is expected since text directives skip transcription and the queued->structuring transition happens on the first poll), then disappeared and the Execution Summary dialog opened at ~10.7s from submit. Sticky banner sits right under the PageHeader with a yellow background, spinner, primary status line and helper text — it does NOT overlay/modal the page (page scroll and filter chips remained clickable while banner was visible). Execution Summary dialog reported '1 task created, 1 person assigned, 1 approval to review' for the __UITEST__ directive.
